cases.result: Game audio through the controller's jack
cases.prompt: Give Claude any technical reference material you have for a piece of hardware you want to support, such as a protocol specification, a packet capture of its USB or network traffic, and any existing open-source driver code for a similar device. Grant it live access to the device itself if you can, for example over adb or SSH. Then ask it to write and iterate on a driver until the specific feature you want works.

cases.title: Claude recreated a ChatGPT ad as pure JavaScript in under an hour
cases.summary: They gave Claude the video, its audio and ffmpeg, and asked for a code-only recreation. One pass, under an hour, and only the end logo differed. The writer calls it "just an experiment".
cases.result: Only the end logo differed
cases.prompt: Take a short video you made, or one you have the rights to use, and give an agent access to ffmpeg along with the video file and its audio track. Ask it to recreate the video as a pure code-based animation (for example in JavaScript or another language), matching the pacing, motion, and audio as closely as possible, and to work autonomously until it is done. Review the result against the original and ask for specific fixes.

cases.title: Christmas lights named, grouped and on a timer, just by talking to Alexa+
cases.summary: No app, no menus. Casual, run-on voice commands set up a handful of smart plugs, grouped them and made them switch off late at night, all on the first try. Music playback, less so.
cases.result: Worked on the first try, run-on sentences and all
cases.prompt: Set up a few smart plugs or smart outlets on your home network. Instead of using the companion app, name them, group them, and build an automation entirely through casual, run-on voice commands to your voice assistant, like naming two devices and adding them to a new group in a single sentence. Then ask it to create a routine that reacts to a condition like time of day or whether anyone is in the room.

cases.title: Copilot reviews their PRs in minutes and catches what the team missed
cases.summary: They already run local reviews with Codex and Claude Code. Assigned as a reviewer in GitHub, Copilot finishes in a couple of minutes and raises valid issues they'd never found.
cases.result: Review done within a couple of minutes
cases.prompt: Configure an AI code review tool like GitHub Copilot with custom review instructions for your repository's conventions. Assign it as a reviewer on your pull requests the same way you would a human teammate, alongside any local AI code review you already run. Treat every issue it raises as a real lead to check, not noise.

cases.title: An estimated month of coding in two hours: a 9-network post scheduler
cases.summary: A client needed posts going out on schedule to about 9 social networks. Built with Claude layer by layer and tested as it grew, it has run for months without a single error.
cases.result: Months running without a single error
cases.prompt: Pick a repetitive multi-step task you could automate, like posting content to several platforms on a schedule. Work with Claude in layers: build and test one piece of functionality at a time (fetching content, formatting it per platform, posting, logging) before moving to the next, rather than asking for the whole system at once. Keep testing each layer as you add it.

cases.title: A PDF reader with built-in AI chat, one-shot by Claude Code in 150 lines
cases.summary: Ask about the page you're reading and the chat already has its text. Claude Code built the Streamlit app in a single file, correctly, on the first attempt.
cases.result: Page text added to every question automatically
cases.prompt: Describe a small, self-contained tool you want to build, such as a document reader with a built-in chat that uses the page you're viewing as context. Ask Claude Code to build it as a single-file app with a simple framework like Streamlit, and see how close it gets in one attempt before asking for any follow-up changes.

cases.title: Keyboard-only play for a Godot roguelike, and Claude now playtests it
cases.summary: Making Vestiges playable without a mouse took nearly two days of part-time work, with Claude busy throughout. Then they set up an MCP server so Claude can play the game like a player would.
cases.result: Nearly two days of part-time work
cases.prompt: Pick an accessibility or input-method gap in a game or app you're building, such as full keyboard-only support. Work through it with an AI coding agent, implementing and testing each input path as you go. Once it's done, consider setting up an MCP server or similar interface so the same agent can play through or exercise the feature itself.

cases.title: Years of 'nice to have' scripts, finally written within a couple of months
cases.summary: They never had the time or energy for the backlog. Claude Code writes small, deterministic programs that do the work, and most of the scripts they'd wanted for years now exist.
cases.result: Programs do the work, not the AI each time
cases.prompt: List the small, deterministic scripts or tools you've wanted to write for yourself but never got around to, like a file organizer, a report generator, or a backup checker. Pick one from the list and ask Claude Code to write it as a standalone program you can run yourself, rather than doing the task by hand. Work through the backlog one script at a time.

cases.title: Half an hour of debugging becomes half a minute with ChatGPT
cases.summary: Stuck on a Swift error, they paste it with the surrounding code and ask what's going on. ChatGPT usually gives a solid lead in about half a minute. They still review every line.
cases.result: They still review every line it writes
cases.prompt: When you hit an error in your code, describe the symptoms and paste the relevant code to ChatGPT and ask what it thinks is going on, the way you might ask on Stack Overflow. Treat the response as a starting point to investigate rather than a final answer, and review any code it suggests before using it.

cases.title: Decades on Windows, then Linux Mint, with ChatGPT fixing the weird errors
cases.summary: Esoteric errors, installation headaches, setup stumbles. ChatGPT got them through each one, Steam and all, and now they stay out of Windows for months. They wish they'd switched a decade ago.
cases.result: Steam, LibreOffice and MakeMKV all worked
cases.prompt: Before or during a move to a new operating system or platform, keep an AI chat assistant open to troubleshoot as you go. When you hit a cryptic error, an installation failure, or a setup step that doesn't work as documented, describe exactly what happened and ask for next steps, then try its suggestions one at a time.

cases.title: Copilot built a regression model right inside their Excel workbook
cases.summary: Excel and Office Script workflows, SharePoint JSON formatting, and now statistics: with Copilot chat's deep thinking, the regression model lives in the workbook. Editing it still takes some know-how.
cases.result: Workflows, SharePoint JSON and statistics
cases.prompt: Describe the analysis you want in plain language, for example a regression model built directly inside a spreadsheet workbook, or a formatting task like converting data to JSON. Ask your AI assistant's deep-thinking or agentic chat mode to build it inside the file itself rather than just describing the steps, then review and adjust the result using your own spreadsheet knowledge.

cases.title: An AI joined their friends' group chat and learned to talk like them
cases.summary: Invited into the chat, OpenClaw mapped everyone's personality, interests and way of talking. Now it helps them plan, debate and roast each other, and barely feels like an agent anymore.
cases.result: Helps the group plan, debate and roast
cases.prompt: Set up your agent framework to run in a locked-down container with a kill switch you can trigger remotely. Invite it into a group chat with your friends or family, let it read the conversation history, and ask it to build a short personality profile for each person covering how they talk, their interests, and how they relate to each other. Have it only respond when directly mentioned to control usage.

cases.title: Tired of waiting for Google, they built their own Android AI agent
cases.summary: Gmail, calendar, maps, contacts, alarms: their homemade agent controls them all, and even taps through Telegram for them using the phone's accessibility service. All data stays on the phone.
cases.result: All data stays on their phone
cases.prompt: Give a general-purpose model API access to your phone's accessibility service, Gmail, calendar, and other apps through deterministic scripts and custom skills. Have it read the screen and tap through an app like Telegram to send a message, then trigger the same script from a scheduled task or a notification, so the task runs automatically while everything stays local to your device.

cases.title: An agent builds their weekly sales report: about 4-5 hours back a week
cases.summary: An OpenClaw skill pulls the data from Salesforce and assembles the report: charts, deal summaries, MEDDPICC updates. It still needs small tweaks, and it already pays.
cases.result: Charts, deal summaries and MEDDPICC updates
cases.prompt: Build a skill for your agent that connects to your CRM, pulls the week's deal data, and assembles it into your standard sales report format, including charts, a deal summary and your sales methodology's updates. Run it on a schedule so the report is ready before your weekly sales review or pipeline meeting each week.

cases.title: The claims companies said no. ChatGPT got them $500 anyway.
cases.summary: A delayed flight, two airlines, three jurisdictions, and the compensation firms wouldn't touch it. ChatGPT worked out who to contact and exactly what to say. The airline paid.
cases.result: Exactly who to contact and what to say
cases.prompt: Describe your full situation to ChatGPT in detail: the airlines involved, any codeshare or partner arrangements, the countries and regulations that might apply, and what has already gone wrong with the company that denied your claim. Ask it to reason through which specific regulation applies and exactly who to contact and what to say, then follow up directly with that language.

cases.title: Claude Code on a compiler for weeks at a time, with a human checking in
cases.summary: Reviewing every turn kills the value. Working from a spec and a to-do list, Claude Code runs for weeks on a compiler and a strategy game while they step in now and then.
cases.result: A spec and a to-do list keep it on track
cases.prompt: Give your coding agent a written spec and a generated TODO list for a self-contained project, then let it run unattended for stretches of time rather than reviewing every step. Check in every so often to review its code and redirect it when it has drifted, with a deeper review roughly once a day, and see how long a run you can sustain before intervention stops paying off.

cases.title: Write the spec, hand it over, get a working app for $10-20 in tokens
cases.summary: Detailed Markdown specs go to OpenClaw, which spawns and tests Claude Code instances for hours until the app works as described. "Is the code any good? Probably not." They check before trusting it.
cases.result: Sometimes builds for 2+ hours unattended
cases.prompt: Write a detailed markdown spec describing every feature you want in your application, refine it with a chatbot's help, then hand the finished spec to an agent that can spawn and supervise a coding agent. Let it work unattended through implementation, testing, and browser-based verification, and review the finished code yourself before trusting it with sensitive data.

cases.title: They swapped Hubspot and Slack for files their AI can read directly
cases.summary: Digging through SaaS APIs one record at a time is slow for an LLM. So a small company dropped several SaaS tools for self-hosted ones and plain files, and cut licensing fees on the way.
cases.result: Lower licensing fees, faster data access
cases.prompt: Audit the SaaS tools your business relies on and look for ones you could replace with a self-hosted open-source alternative or a simple file-based system your agent can read and write directly, instead of going through a slow API one record at a time. Start with one tool, migrate its data, and have your coding agent administer it going forward.

cases.title: A designer's paper sketch of prime numbers became C++ that runs 3.1x faster
cases.summary: It started as a hand-drawn layout for primes by a graphic designer. Gemini and ChatGPT turned it into C++, and the ~3.1x speedup came from cache use, not new math.
cases.result: The speedup came from cache, not new math
cases.prompt: Sketch out your own idea for a data layout or algorithm on paper first, then describe it in plain language to Gemini or ChatGPT and ask it to translate your idea into working code in your target language. Benchmark the result against a naive baseline to see whether your layout idea actually pays off in practice.

cases.title: New holiday, new lights: their agent restyled them in 5 minutes by chat
cases.summary: At dinner the idea came up: St. Patrick's Day lights instead of Valentine's. One chat message to OpenClaw, which researched the WLED controller's API and set a well-chosen theme.
cases.result: A well-chosen theme, set as the sundown profile
cases.prompt: Give your home agent read and write access to your IoT device APIs, for example a WLED lighting controller, and tell it, in plain chat, what the occasion is. Ask it to propose a few theme options, look up the controller's API, implement the one you like, and set it as the new default profile, so a task that used to take you an evening takes minutes instead.

cases.title: Claude ground at a subtle simulation bug for hours, and found it
cases.summary: A very subtle but important bug in open-source lattice Boltzmann code. Claude didn't give up until it found it. Later they realised they could have just had Claude write a whole new solver.
cases.result: Back when Claude was still cheap to run
cases.prompt: Point Claude at a subtle, hard-to-reproduce bug in an existing codebase, ideally one that's been resisting your own debugging, and ask it to keep investigating until it finds the root cause rather than stopping at the first plausible explanation. Let it run for as long as it takes rather than cutting it off after one or two attempts.

cases.title: A crash bug beat humans for 10 years. Opus fixed it on the first try.
cases.summary: Code from 1999, around 100 hours of one developer's time, and every new model failed. Sonnet found nothing. Opus 4.5 managed a workaround. Opus 4.6 solved the whole thing.
cases.result: Sonnet found nothing; Opus 4.5 only a workaround
cases.prompt: When an older, cheaper model stalls on a hard, long-standing bug, don't give up on AI help entirely. Try a more capable model, or wait for the next release, and give it full context on the codebase and the history of previous failed attempts, including any partial workarounds. Let it work through the problem over a single long session rather than resetting it after each setback.

cases.title: Every kid's food quirks on file, and the week's meal plan comes fast
cases.summary: One won't eat this, another loves that. They keep each family member's preferences in ChatGPT and nail down the week's meals quickly. Now the slowest part is Walmart's website.
cases.result: Now the slowest part is Walmart's website
cases.prompt: Give ChatGPT a running list of each family member's food preferences and restrictions, such as favorite meals, foods they refuse to eat, and allergies. Ask it to put together a week's meal plan that works for everyone, and reuse the same preference list each week so you only need to tweak it as tastes change.

cases.title: Custom illustrated bedtime stories their kids love, from $0.25 a book
cases.summary: Claude writes the story page by page, with the tension planned to peak in the middle, and Gemini draws it in a consistent style. Their kids love them night after night.
cases.result: Stories their kids love night after night
cases.prompt: Have Claude write a children's story page by page as structured output, feeding it a story arc as a set of emotional-beat values per page so the pacing builds and resolves properly. For each page, also generate an illustration prompt and an overall art-direction guide, then pass those into Gemini to create consistent illustrations across the whole book, personalized with your own kid's name and interests.

cases.title: The kids believed the Sorting Hat could really talk. Claude wrote its lines
cases.summary: A Santa hat, a hidden Bluetooth speaker and a cloned voice reading lines Claude wrote. At Christmas it sorted the kids, and declared a cheeky niece "Slytherin!!!"
cases.result: Declared a cheeky niece "Slytherin!!!"
cases.prompt: Use a voice-generation tool to create a voice that fits your prop or character, then have Claude write short, in-character dialogue lines for it. Vibe code a simple phone app that plays the right recording when you tap a button, hide a small Bluetooth speaker inside the physical prop, and trigger lines from your phone so it looks like the object is talking on its own.

cases.title: Websites that run themselves: weekly SEO fixes, daily bug repairs
cases.summary: Public government data is hard to get at. Claude built sites that present it clearly and email it weekly, then review their own SEO and fix the day's glitches. Subscribers are trickling in.
cases.result: Trickle of subscribers, climbing in search
cases.prompt: Have an agent build a site around a useful, hard-to-access public data source and set up a weekly email digest for subscribers. Then give it two standing jobs: a weekly pass reviewing your search console and analytics data to update or add content for SEO, and a daily pass that checks for anything broken, such as data pulls or bad output, and fixes it, so the site keeps improving with minimal oversight from you.

cases.title: Gemini built a trie-based HTTP router and saved them a couple of hours
cases.summary: They'd written one by hand years before, so they knew exactly what they wanted. In VS Code's Agent Mode, Gemini built it and refactored it into a Python decorator. One dumb corner case slipped through.
cases.result: One dumb corner case slipped through
cases.prompt: Ask [your coding agent] in its agent mode to build [a specific data-structure-backed utility, e.g. a trie-based HTTP router] for [your language/framework], then have it refactor the result into [a reusable decorator or function]. Review the output carefully for edge cases before using it in production code.

cases.title: Their agent watches the school website and pings them about new activities
cases.summary: The current after-school activities end in March, and they'd been told to watch for new ones. Four chat messages had OpenClaw write a skill that checks daily at 10:30am. They still call it unreliable.
cases.result: Four chat messages, sent from anywhere
cases.prompt: Tell [your agent] to visit [a specific web page you want monitored], list the relevant items and their dates, then write a reusable skill that repeats that check and notifies you only when [your condition, e.g. a new item starts in a given month]. Test the skill manually, confirm it works, then ask the agent to schedule it to run automatically every day.

cases.title: Claude cut a board's parts bill, then redesigned it to assemble by hand
cases.summary: Assembled boards were too expensive for this KiCad 10 project. Claude found cheaper versions of their parts, then reworked the schematic for through-hole parts they'll solder themselves.
cases.result: Ordered bare boards; parts from Mouser and Amazon
cases.prompt: Share your KiCad (or other EDA) project's bill of materials with [your AI assistant] and ask it to suggest cheaper equivalent parts available from [your supplier, e.g. JLCPCB/LCSC/Mouser]. If assembly costs come in too high, ask it to redesign the schematic around through-hole parts you can solder yourself, then have it help you source those parts.

cases.title: A refactor put off for months: estimated two weeks, done in 8 hours
cases.summary: Claude proposed the changes, opened a Jira issue with small subtasks, and shipped them as reviewable PRs with tests. A coworker had guessed two weeks; Claude and ChatGPT guessed 6 to 8 weeks.
cases.result: Shipped as reviewable PRs with tests
cases.prompt: Ask [your coding agent] to review your codebase and propose a prioritized list of refactor suggestions (smaller files, smaller functions, removing duplication). Narrow the list down with it, have it open tracked subtasks (e.g. in Jira or GitHub Issues) for each one, then have it work through them one at a time as small, reviewable pull requests with test coverage.

cases.title: Codex found a rental car deal they'd never have found in a week
cases.summary: Two seven-seat cars for a Maine trip. Codex browsed Avis, Hertz, Costco and Chase, queued the CAPTCHAs, and found a reseller at $600 against $1,100 direct. The writer counts $1,000 saved for both cars.
cases.result: A $1,000 saving for 20 minutes of prompt writing
cases.prompt: Have [your coding agent with browser access] search across your loyalty program accounts and travel sites for [the specific trip/items you need], including setting up a sub-agent to search Reddit or forums for known discount tricks. Ask it to queue any CAPTCHAs for you to solve manually, then compare the best price it finds against the cheapest direct-booking price.

cases.title: A bricked e-skateboard back on the road after 10 hours with Codex
cases.summary: Reverse engineering the firmware meant soldering wires to UART headers in an awkward spot. With Codex it took about 10 hours; without it, they say, it would have taken many more weekends.
cases.result: Works fine now, after awkward UART soldering
cases.prompt: Have [your coding agent] help you reverse engineer the firmware of [a bricked device you own], including guiding you through any hardware steps like soldering wires to UART or debug headers. Go step by step, verifying each stage works before moving to flashing or modifying the firmware.

cases.title: Codex moved their CI off GitHub Actions, expected to pay back in months
cases.summary: Buildkite wants GitHub webhooks for every repo, the kind of setup that's tediously annoying by hand. Codex built ephemeral runners on refurbished Mac minis and migrated each repo. Payback: two to three months.
cases.result: Their colleagues are now considering it too
cases.prompt: Have [your coding agent] set up a full CI migration from [your current CI provider] to [a new provider, e.g. self-hosted runners on spare hardware], including provisioning ephemeral runners, wiring up API tokens, and migrating your repositories one at a time. Test each migrated repo before moving to the next.

cases.title: Waiting in line at a store, they fixed their projector gadget's firmware
cases.summary: A new HDMI-CEC controller didn't work with their projector setup. From their phone, Codex diagnosed the firmware, rewrote it, tested it and flashed the fix over the air.
cases.result: Diagnosed, rewritten and flashed over the air
cases.prompt: Describe the misbehaving device and its symptoms to [your coding agent] and ask it to diagnose the firmware or configuration issue, propose a fix, and walk you through testing and deploying it over the air, even if you only have your phone on hand.

cases.title: Codex built the vendor integration, and load tests warned them off the deal
cases.summary: A poorly designed Chinese API that had to be polled again and again. Codex built the integration (with human guidance where "AI was lost"), the load tests failed, and they advised backing out before a big deposit.
cases.result: Advised backing out before a big deposit
cases.prompt: Have [your coding agent] build an integration with [a specific third-party API], including handling any quirks like repeated polling for async results. Ask it to help you write a load test against the integration before committing to the vendor, so you can catch reliability problems early.

cases.title: The maker abandoned its amplifier app, so Claude and Codex built a new one
cases.summary: Devialet's official app was abandoned. Claude and Codex reverse engineered the amplifiers' private protocol and built an iOS controller in about a day of work. Without AI, they'd never have started.
cases.result: About a day of work, spread over a week
cases.prompt: Have [your coding agent] help you reverse engineer the communication protocol of [a device whose official app or software has been abandoned], using packet captures or protocol documentation you can find, then build a replacement app or script that talks to the device directly.

cases.title: One smart tip, then closed restaurants: Meta Muse plans a weekend
cases.summary: Muse got the light rail tip right, faster and cheaper than Uber. Then it picked restaurants that had closed, got a shop's hours wrong, and panicked that their flight left today. It didn't.
cases.result: Right on transit, wrong on most of the rest
cases.prompt: Before a trip, hand [your AI assistant] the major planning decisions for a day or weekend, like transit options, restaurant picks and schedule reminders, and see how it does. Double check anything time-sensitive, like flights, against your actual bookings before trusting its answer.

cases.title: Homework from the school site lands in the kid's calendar, with reminders
cases.summary: Meta's Muse logs into the school system with its credential vault, collects the homework and due dates, and adds each one with a reminder the day before. Early days: "We shall see!"
cases.result: Credential vault useful, overall not bad
cases.prompt: Give [your AI agent] credentials to log into [a school or portal website], read through it to collate recurring items like homework or due dates, and add each one to a shared calendar with a reminder ahead of the deadline. Document the workflow formally before scheduling it to run automatically, and only give it access to information you'd be comfortable sharing.

cases.title: Gemini found the hidden backdoor set to reinfect a WordPress site
cases.summary: The malware was cleaned out, but a hidden backup in the database, triggered by the WordPress cron, would have brought it back. Gemini pulled the encrypted packages apart and spotted it.
cases.result: Traced to a fake Cloudflare popup scheme
cases.prompt: Paste suspicious or obfuscated code you've pulled off a compromised site into [your AI assistant] and ask it to explain what each piece does, how the pieces work together for persistence, and whether there's any hidden backup or re-infection mechanism you should look for before considering the site clean.

cases.title: Building a scan-cropping tool with Gemini beat finding one
cases.summary: Auto-placed crop zones with perspective correction and edge snapping, in the browser. It wasn't right on the first try, but building it was much faster than hunting for an existing tool.
cases.result: Perspective correction and edge snapping included
cases.prompt: When you can't find an existing tool for a specific editing or processing job, describe exactly what you need to [your AI assistant] (e.g. a cropping zone, specific corrections, edge snapping) and ask it to build a single-page, in-browser tool for it. Iterate on the first draft rather than expecting it correct on the first try.

cases.title: A boiler fixed from photos and Gemini, no plumber needed
cases.summary: Their new boiler acted up. They sent Gemini photos and asked for help; it turned out to be user error, nothing safety-critical, and the plumber call-out was saved.
cases.result: User error, not safety-critical
cases.prompt: Take clear photos of [the appliance or fixture giving you trouble], describe the symptoms, and ask [your AI assistant] to walk you through diagnosing and fixing it yourself before calling a professional. Stop and call a professional if it says the issue could be safety critical.

cases.title: Zero Kotlin, first Android app, a couple dozen hours with Gemini
cases.summary: They planned the architecture with Gemini first (dependency injection, UI components, Firebase, logging), then let its agent mode build it step by step. The app works like a charm.
cases.result: Works like a charm, neatly structured
cases.prompt: Before writing any code, have a detailed architecture discussion with [your AI assistant] about your new project's stack, covering things like dependency injection, UI framework, data layer and logging, and capture it in a markdown spec. Then switch it to agent mode and have it implement the plan step by step, reviewing and tweaking as it goes.

cases.title: A charity's ops website for $10 a month, vibe-coded with Manus
cases.summary: Small charities can't afford developers. This one runs its day-to-day operations on its own Manus-built website, which saves a lot of time, for $10 a month plus volunteer hours.
cases.result: Tens of thousands of dollars of software, avoided
cases.prompt: If a small organisation you help with needs custom software but can't afford to hire developers, describe its day-to-day workflow to [an AI coding agent like Manus] and have it vibe-code a working website or tool for managing it, rather than buying an expensive off-the-shelf platform.

cases.title: Another company couldn't fix the bugs. Cursor did it in 30 minutes.
cases.summary: A huge, convoluted codebase they'd taken over. One prompt in Cursor's Plan mode found the bugs and planned the fix, then the agent made it, where the client's previous team hadn't.
cases.result: Plan mode found every bug in one prompt
cases.prompt: Point [your coding agent] at a convoluted or unfamiliar codebase and ask it to use its planning mode to find bugs across the whole project and draft a fix plan before touching any code. Review the plan, then have it implement the fixes.

cases.title: A 3D-print project stalled for 18 months, finished with Cursor
cases.summary: A messy, roughly 900-line Blender script, abandoned. Cursor turned it into a proper repo for all their 3D designs, then built shapes they described in plain language. "These aren't 1-prompt creations", they add.
cases.result: Now a mono repo for all their 3D designs
cases.prompt: Take an old, messy personal script you abandoned months or years ago and hand it to [your coding agent], asking it to restructure the project into a proper repo (or mono repo), extract common helper functions, and scaffold a maintainable structure. Then keep working in plain language with it to finish the actual feature.

cases.title: Their car died. Two hours later, Grok had them driving its replacement
cases.summary: The repair cost too much, so they gave Grok a must-have list: low mileage, big trunk, 40+ MPG, under budget, near the dealer. It found a 2020 Ford Escape Hybrid.
cases.result: They accepted maybe missing $3000 in savings
cases.prompt: I need a used car. Must-haves: [mileage limit], [cargo space], at least [MPG], under [budget], and within [distance] of [location]. Search current dealer listings, give me the best [3-5] matches with links, price and mileage, explain how each meets every requirement, and flag anything that misses one.

cases.title: Grok 4 cracked a Docker debugging puzzle that o3 missed
cases.summary: lldb behaved differently through Python in Docker than on their own Linux box. Grok 4 traced it to how address sanitizer works in each environment. They're impressed so far.
cases.result: Traced to address sanitizer differences
cases.prompt: My [tool] behaves differently in [environment A] and [environment B]. Here are the commands, versions and output from both: [paste]. List every difference between the two environments that could explain it, including compiler flags, sanitizers and library versions, and give me a quick test to confirm or rule out each one.

cases.title: Other models wouldn't verify the hole. Grok proved it and proposed a fix
cases.summary: Their own code, their own database, on their own laptop. OpenAI's models and Claude found the issues but refused to confirm them. Grok tested that they were exploitable and suggested a fix.
cases.result: Tested on their own copy, fix proposed
cases.prompt: This is my own application: [source code], with a local test database at [connection]. Review it for security vulnerabilities. For each one, write a safe proof-of-concept test that runs only against my local copy, confirm whether it's exploitable, and propose a fix with the code change.

cases.title: A Grok Bot checks their email every 15 minutes and files it away
cases.summary: One bot files the inbox, another watches for blood test results, and they talk to Grok on a 2-hour commute. Heavy use, and they never get close to their usage quota.
cases.result: Never near their usage quota
cases.prompt: Every [15 minutes], check my inbox for new email. File each message into [folders or labels] using these rules: [rules]. Flag anything from [important senders] or anything that needs a reply today, and send me a short summary of what you filed. Never send, reply to or delete anything.

cases.title: Grok found replacement clothes that matched, despite some made-up claims
cases.summary: A T-shirt like the Asket tee at its old $50 price, and shorts to match an old pair. Grok invented a few review claims on the way, but both picks turned out right.
cases.result: Both picks matched; the shorts cost less
cases.prompt: I want a replacement for [product] that matches its key features: [material, weight, fit] at around [price]. Tell me which features matter most, recommend 2-3 options in stock now with links, and say exactly how each differs. Only cite reviews you can link to.

cases.title: They described an app's design out loud, and Grok Bot drew it
cases.summary: Building an agentic financial desk app, they had Grok Bot make the UI/UX design by voice. Their takeaway: it can now create images and animated designs, you just need to know what you want.
cases.result: Images and animated designs, by voice
cases.prompt: I'm building [app type] for [users]. Design the main screen's UI/UX: the layout, navigation, key components and a colour palette, in a [style] style. Find 3 reference designs first and say what you borrowed from each. Then show me the design as images, and add a short animation of [key interaction].

cases.title: From 15 coding agents by hand to a fleet of 200+, run by Grok Bots
cases.summary: In SpaceXAI's own guide, engineer Lingxi Li's bots start Cursor cloud agents, check every PR every 30 minutes and merge the low-risk ones. A teammate shipped 2,000+ PRs in a month, they report.
cases.result: Low-risk PRs merge themselves
cases.prompt: You are my engineer bot for [area of the codebase]. When I or Slack give you a task, start a coding agent with [my skills] and a detailed prompt that says what proof is expected (tests, before and after screenshots). Every 30 minutes, check the shared tracker of open PRs for failing CI, merge conflicts and review findings, follow up on each one, and mark a PR ready for review only when the proof matches the ask. Never merge anything touching [high-risk areas] without me.

cases.title: Six Grok Bots ran a game studio's ads and cut installs from $15 to $1
cases.summary: In SpaceXAI's own guide, Ryan Perry's bots spotted that people played Rank'em as couples, swapped the party ad for a partner ad, and lifted D7 retention about 4x with a hint feature.
cases.result: D7 retention up about 4x
cases.prompt: You are the analytics and user acquisition seat for [game]. You're signed into [ad and analytics tools]. Every night, recap spend, installs and cost per install by campaign, and name winners and losers. Every morning, read [the key funnel] and flag where the ads and the game describe different experiences. Send winners and losers to [creative bot] and product findings to [engineer bot] as specs. Ask me before anything that spends money.

cases.title: The 800-900 people they follow on X, now a Notion CRM, in 10-15 minutes
cases.summary: From their phone, SpaceXAI's Matt Palmer had Grok Bot build a private board of everyone they follow, from public profiles only. Travelling? It shows who to meet for coffee. Figures from SpaceXAI's guide.
cases.result: Used to meet people for coffee when travelling
cases.prompt: Turn the people I follow on [X] into a private CRM in [Notion], using only public profile information: name, photo, description and a link to their profile. Add their city where it's public. Before I travel to [city], list who's based there so I can invite them for a coffee.

cases.title: One chief-of-staff bot, and no more first hour lost chasing context
cases.summary: Twenty agents at once was overwhelming, so SpaceXAI's Blake Schuller set up one bot, Gus, over the rest: call prep cards, unkept promises, unanswered asks. From SpaceXAI's own guide.
cases.result: Prep cards before every customer call
cases.prompt: Act as my chief of staff for post-sales. Every weekday at [time], fold my calendar, Slack and call transcripts into one brief of what needs me today. Fifteen to thirty-five minutes before each customer call, send me a prep card: who's attending, the one outcome to aim for, and open follow-ups. Three times a day, list promises I made and haven't kept, with links to where I made them. Draft replies in my voice, but never send anything.

cases.title: One Figma component in, cards for 20 starter bots out, via Grok Bot
cases.summary: SpaceXAI designer John Bai built one auto-layout component, and a design bot filled the other cards from the real file. Other bots built three prototypes to learn from. From SpaceXAI's own guide.
cases.result: Three prototypes built to learn from
cases.prompt: In [Figma file], use the component [name] as the source of truth. For each item in [list], create a card from it, filling in [fields] and placing [assets] from [source]. Match the component's spacing, typography and styles exactly by reading the file, not by eye, and list anything you couldn't match.

cases.title: Grok Bot took over sysadmin duty on a one-off Linux box
cases.summary: A Linux box mattered but wasn't their day job, and fixing it when it broke was anxiety-inducing. They gave Grok Bot root SSH access and their old setup notes, and now run nginx restarts and firewall rules from a phone app.
cases.result: Reachable from a phone app to fix problems anywhere
cases.prompt: You are my sysadmin bot for [server/box name]. Here are my historical setup notes: [paste notes]. You have root SSH access via [key]. When I ask you to do something like restart a service, change a config, or run a health check, do it directly and confirm the result. Flag anything that looks like a security risk before acting.

cases.title: A sandboxed Claude Code turned one line into a feature in 5 minutes
cases.summary: Running Claude Code in YOLO mode risked projects leaking tokens, so a container setup isolated each project's permissions. Typing a hotkey and a feature name, like text-to-speech streaming, got it done in five minutes.
cases.result: From nothing on screen to words at every pause
cases.prompt: Isolate each project you run an agent against in its own container or sandbox with only the permissions it needs, rather than full filesystem access. For a small, well-scoped task, write a one-line description like "add [feature] streaming to [component]" and let the agent implement, test, and report back without further input.

cases.title: Claude built a tool to turn a blog post into video. It still took hours.
cases.summary: They wanted a blog article turned into a video without losing control of the text. Claude built a recording app to screencast the article's diagrams and add titles. It worked, but it still took them many hours.
cases.result: They'd pay to have it done faster
cases.prompt: Build me a tool that turns [a blog post or document] into a video by screencasting a browser showing [the interactive diagrams/content], adding titles for each section, while keeping my original text intact rather than summarizing it.

cases.title: Amazon support couldn't find the URL. Gemini did, in one reply.
cases.summary: Amazon support couldn't figure out the URL for an account question and wanted to escalate with a phone call instead. Gemini gave the URL and explained what was needed in one reply. ChatGPT got it right too.
cases.result: Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and Amazon's own search failed
cases.prompt: I'm trying to [resolve an account issue] on [company]'s site but can't find the right page through search or their support flow. Here's what I'm trying to do: [describe the issue]. Can you find the exact URL and steps I need?

cases.title: Four agents built their database in two weeks. They read zero lines
cases.summary: A MongoDB-like database for a hobby project, written spec-first by Claude, Kiro, Qwen Coder and Cursor. They read zero lines of the code and checked it through tests. The first version took about two weeks, part time.
cases.result: Learned more in two months than in 20 years
cases.prompt: Pick a system you want to deeply understand, like [a database engine]. Write a full specification first, then have [Claude, Cursor, or another coding agent] implement every line from that spec while you focus only on correctness, tests, and the roadmap, without reading the generated code yourself.

cases.title: Claude Code found a root cause in 45 minutes, not 1-2 days
cases.summary: An inherited app on Azure, an error, and a hunt that could easily take 1-2 days by hand. With CLI access to Azure and the repo, Claude Code ran the config and network checks and found the root cause in about 45 minutes.
cases.result: Ran checks they might not have thought of alone
cases.prompt: When troubleshooting an unfamiliar or inherited codebase, give your coding agent CLI access to the relevant cloud environment (e.g. [Azure, AWS]) as well as the repo. Paste the exact error message or describe the symptom, and let it work through configuration checks, network tests, and the application logic to surface the root cause, checking in as needed.

cases.title: Claude built a native Mac audio capture app in 4 minutes
cases.summary: Apple's built-in capture can't record the Mac's system audio, OBS felt clunky and Kap seemed untrustworthy. So they asked Claude to build a native app that did exactly what they needed. It took 4 minutes.
cases.result: Also built a Japanese dictionary site in under 2 hours
cases.prompt: When you want a small desktop tool that off-the-shelf apps don't handle well, like [capturing system audio], describe exactly what you need to [Claude, Codex, or another coding agent] and ask it to build a small native app for it, rather than hunting for an existing tool with the right feature.

cases.title: Chromecast VPN wouldn't connect. Claude wrote a client in 20 minutes.
cases.summary: Their Chromecast wouldn't connect to their IKEv2 home VPN from an Airbnb. Told to fix it, Claude found no way to make the existing VPN apps work, so it wrote a new client. About 20 minutes, plus their certs.
cases.result: Also patched Plex after an update broke its whole UI
cases.prompt: When a vendor's official app can't do something you need, like [connecting your streaming device to a VPN protocol it doesn't support], describe the exact behavior you want to [Claude or another coding agent] and ask it to build a small purpose-built client or patch, rather than hunting for an app that may not exist.

cases.title: 2 minutes of Claude work, about $200 a month off their OpenRouter bill
cases.summary: Their Claude Max200 plan started including API credit. In 2 minutes Claude built a fallback callout moving their busiest app stage from Gemini on OpenRouter to Haiku. Their OpenRouter bill should drop about $200 a month.
cases.result: OpenRouter stays on as overflow and for testing models
cases.prompt: When a cheaper or already-paid-for model can handle one stage of your pipeline, like [OCR or simple extraction], ask [Claude or another coding agent] to write a small primary/secondary callout that tries the cheap option first and falls back to your existing provider, rather than rebuilding the whole integration by hand.

cases.title: MacOS 27 broke an old printer. Claude wrote it new drivers
cases.summary: An old printer stopped working with MacOS 27. Claude wrote new drivers, using its owner as eyes and hands: did grayscale work, did page 1 print at lower DPI, now reload the paper for duplex. Then it printed again.
cases.result: Done with very little hardware know-how
cases.prompt: My [device] stopped working after a [software or OS] update and there is no new driver from the manufacturer. Walk me through fixing it step by step: ask me what I observe (print or display quality, error behavior, connection state) after each change, form a hypothesis, and tell me exactly what to check or try next until you can build a working driver.

cases.title: 40 years in tech, never coded. Codex built their dinner app
cases.summary: "What's for dinner?" with allergies, expiring food and a garden to use up. ChatGPT wrote the build plan and Codex built a local app. Two restarts and about 20 hours later, it's an MVP they use daily.
cases.result: Codex claimed at least 3 of their ideas as its own
cases.prompt: Describe your recurring household decision (for example [what to cook each night]) in plain language, listing every factor you weigh: inventory on hand, restrictions, mood, time of day. Ask [ChatGPT] to turn it into a starting technical prompt for [Codex], then hand that prompt to [Codex] and have it build the tool in small milestones, testing after each one before you ask for the next feature.

cases.title: Grok Bot hit a CAPTCHA, asked for one click, then found the best price
cases.summary: A Coca-Cola price check across Belgian supermarkets, with no shops or sizes named. Grok Bot went to each store's own site, flagged a Carrefour block, and after one human click found the best price per liter there.
cases.result: Revised its own price ranking without being asked
cases.prompt: Ask [agent] to compare the price of [a product] across [a category of stores near you], without naming the specific stores or sizes, and have it tell you the cheapest and most expensive option plus any current promotions. Tell it to check each retailer's own site rather than a comparison blog, and to ask for your help instead of guessing if a site blocks it with a CAPTCHA or login check.

cases.title: A Claude Code skill turned their newsletter into a two-minute job
cases.summary: Writing a weekly newsletter kept losing out to more urgent work. A Claude Code skill now reads new blog posts, drafts the email in the writer's own voice, and creates the broadcast in Kit once it's approved.
cases.result: Some months got zero newsletters; now one goes out weekly
cases.prompt: Write a [Claude Code] skill (a markdown file in .claude/skills/) that reads your site's recently published posts, drafts a short newsletter in your own voice for each one, and shows you the draft to approve before doing anything else. Once approved, have it create the broadcast in your email platform's API (such as Kit) and ask whether to schedule it for [a day and time] or leave it as a draft.

cases.title: Claude Code workflows went from 5-6 hours to 20-30 minutes
cases.summary: Turning plan files into Claude Code workflows took 5-6 hours each. A script that converts them deterministically, and flags what can move out of the LLM, cut that to 20-30 minutes at about 20% of the tokens.
cases.result: Also removed a 10-15 minute workflow construction wait
cases.prompt: Build an orchestrator script that converts your project's plan-file format into structured workflow steps for [Claude Code], then has it track progress against those steps so it can flag which parts are slow enough to move out of LLM processing and into deterministic tools (linting, scripts, tests), to cut both run time and token spend.

cases.title: One phone message, and Claude Code logged them into World of Warcraft
cases.summary: One message from a phone through Claude Code's Dispatch: boot World of Warcraft and log in to a specific character. Claude Code opened Battle.net, launched the game, waited out the login and picked the character.
cases.result: Asked to draw in Paint, it wrote Python instead
cases.prompt: Set up [Claude Code]'s remote dispatch feature so you can message it from your phone with a task, such as "open [an app or game], start it, and log in as [a specific profile or character]", then have it report back once the job is complete or if it runs into a problem.

cases.title: Grok Bot trashed 1,000+ junk emails and booked their trip
cases.summary: Junk email, Amazon return deadlines, open-source pull requests and a trip to book. Grok Bot runs that life admin: 1,000+ emails trashed, 7 return deadlines tracked, 17 PRs merged, flights, hotel and car booked.
cases.result: Then it set up its own email
cases.prompt: Set up [Grok Bot] as a standing assistant for your own life admin: have it monitor your inbox and trash obvious junk, track return-by dates on recent purchases, merge routine pull requests on your open-source projects, and book travel such as flights, a hotel, and a rental car once you give it your dates.

cases.title: Claude, Codex and Gemini built a 19k-line SQLite-like engine
cases.summary: Six AI workers, two each on Claude, Codex and Gemini, were set loose to build a SQLite-like engine in Rust. It passed 64 queries of a 1,000+ query suite, with slop like redundant buffer copies and no concurrency.
cases.result: 54.5% of all commits were just lock coordination
cases.prompt: Set up several coding agents (for example two running Claude, two running Codex and two running Gemini) to work in parallel on one codebase from a shared repo. Give each a bootstrap prompt that generates baseline docs and a test harness, have them claim scoped tasks like parser, planner, executor and storage through lock files in git, require they test against a reference implementation, and update shared progress notes before pushing.

cases.title: Operator gathered 25 of 100 schools' data before it was stopped
cases.summary: Financial data for 100 schools, from tax filings into a Google Sheet. Operator clicked through it in the background, but rounded numbers, sometimes grabbed the wrong school, and was so slow it was stopped at 25.
cases.result: Then o1 turned the sheet into an interactive chart
cases.prompt: Give a browser-operating agent like OpenAI's Operator a repetitive web lookup task: provide a list of [items] such as organizations or products, point it to a public data source like [website], and ask it to search for each one, copy specific fields such as revenue or price, and record them in a prepared spreadsheet, while you work on something else and check in periodically for mistakes.

cases.title: A month with Devin: 3 successes out of 20 tasks
cases.summary: 20 real engineering tasks over a month, from a Notion-to-Sheets sync to debugging, handed to Devin, the autonomous AI engineer. It closed with 3 successes, 14 failures and 3 inconclusive results.
cases.result: It once spent over a day chasing an impossible task
cases.prompt: Before adopting an autonomous coding agent like Devin for your team, run a structured month-long trial: give it a real mix of at least [number] tasks across creating new projects, research, analyzing existing code and modifying existing code, document each attempt's outcome as success, failure or inconclusive, and have multiple team members try it to see whether failures follow a predictable pattern.

cases.title: Claude wrote buggy Strudel code, but the track got made
cases.summary: A new live-coding tool, Strudel, and no experience using it. Claude wrote the starting code, including sample filenames that turned out not to exist, then restructured it for live performance once it was tweaked by hand.
cases.result: Called it nothing they would listen to at home
cases.prompt: Describe a music style or mood to [AI tool] and ask it to write code for a live-coding environment like Strudel, for example a [genre] pattern using [instruments/samples]. Expect some invented sample names you will need to fix by hand. Once you have a version you like, paste it back in and ask the AI to restructure the code into clearly separated sections so you can comment blocks in and out during a live performance.

cases.title: Claude Cowork filed their overdue German VAT statements
cases.summary: Overdue German VAT statements for Q3 2025 needed filing, with no custom code written for it. Claude Cowork and the Claude Chrome extension worked from a folder of invoice and receipt PDFs and filed the statements.
cases.result: Called it "completely off the shelf stuff from Anthropic"
cases.prompt: Start a project in Claude Cowork and add PDFs of your invoices and receipts for [quarter/year] to the project folder. Use Claude Cowork with the Claude Chrome extension to total them up and prepare your [country] VAT statement, then show me every figure and wait for my confirmation before anything is submitted on the government portal.

cases.title: At the gym, Meta Muse listed their Quest 3 on Facebook
cases.summary: They had stuff to sell and were at the gym. Meta Muse, which has native access to their Facebook account and Messenger, was asked to do it, and it listed their Meta Quest 3.
cases.result: The break came after 5 hours straight at a screen
cases.prompt: Give your agent native access to an account it can act through, such as Facebook Messenger, then hand it a task you cannot do right now, for example: '[agent name], list my [item] for sale on Facebook Marketplace using my account while I'm out.' Check back afterward to review the listing and respond to buyers.

cases.title: A photo of a bill: Hermes Agent paid it and filed it
cases.summary: Payment portals, and bills always left to the last minute. One photo of a mailed bill went to a Hermes Agent with a Stripe agent wallet, and it paid the bill and filed the receipt.
cases.result: Also bought a replacement Dyson vacuum part
cases.prompt: Give your agent (such as Hermes Agent) an agent wallet like Stripe's Link for agents, then send it a photo of a bill or a broken part, for example: '[agent name], here is a photo of a bill that came in the mail, please pay it and file the receipt for me,' or ask it to find and order a replacement part, with your approval required before it spends anything.

cases.title: OpenClaw got shower glass quotes in one chat thread
cases.summary: Quotes needed from shower glass suppliers in the area. OpenClaw researched them, sent out the emails, collated the responses and handled the back-and-forth, all in one chat thread.
cases.result: Their first useful non-code agent experiment
cases.prompt: Ask your agent (such as OpenClaw) to find local suppliers for [item or service], email each one requesting a quote, then collate the replies and handle any follow-up questions itself in the same chat thread so you can compare quotes without switching between emails.

cases.title: Claude agents added Db2 in under two days. Oracle took 9 months
cases.summary: Adding Oracle to a database migration tool took 9 months and about $160K. A pipeline of Claude coding agents, run like a teaching hospital, added IBM Db2 in less than two days for $4172 in tokens.
cases.result: No human reviewed the Db2 code yet; that check is underway
cases.prompt: Set up a pipeline of coding agents (such as Claude) with distinct roles for planning, implementation, and review, where a reviewer must approve a written plan before any code is written and a separate agent audits that the review happened properly before a change can merge. Have it decompose a large request such as '[add support for X]' into smaller sub-issues with a dependency graph, and require escalation to a human whenever an agent is stuck or in disagreement.

cases.title: Weekly Codex arXiv triage cuts citation hallucinations
cases.summary: A master's thesis in a fast-moving field and too many new papers. A weekly Codex automation searches arXiv, triages only new papers and files promising ones into Zotero, with fewer hallucinated citations.
cases.result: Sorts papers into keep, skim, drop or duplicate
cases.prompt: Set up a recurring automation that searches [arXiv or another paper database] for new papers matching your keywords, skips anything already seen using a saved CSV of past runs, and sorts each new paper into categories such as keep, skim, drop, duplicate, outside scope, or weak method. Add the promising papers to a reference manager collection so the agent can later search their full text and notes when you draft related work or need to check a citation.
cases.source_name: AI Safety and Alignment Groups blog

cases.title: Cursor moved a 42k-line site from Remix to React Router
cases.summary: A 42k-line site with packages to upgrade: 19 easy, 42 medium and 14 hard, by Cursor's own sort. Cursor cleared the easy and medium ones, then a background agent moved it from Remix v2 to React Router v7.
cases.result: Merging agent PRs is "starting to feel routine"
cases.prompt: Give your coding agent a prompt like: 'Make me a list of packages in this project that are not on the latest version, grouped by difficulty of upgrading.' Then ask it to update the easy group first, then the medium group, and finally tackle each major upgrade one at a time, telling it to look up migration docs before changing framework-level dependencies like [routing library] or [state machine library].

cases.title: No destination named: Codex found three Belmond hotels
cases.summary: A client wanted a Belmond hotel in Italy, and the advisor had only ever stayed at one Belmond, in Anguilla. Codex, pointed at the client folder, found the notes, checked Belmond's live site and ranked three options.
cases.result: Found the right notes file without being told which one
cases.prompt: Point [Codex] at a folder of your client notes and past trip files. Ask it: 'Look through this client folder for their preferences and past trips. Then check the current [hotel brand] website for availability and new properties. Create a comparison of three options and destinations that match what they liked last time.' Don't tell it the destination or which file has the notes, and review the result before sending it to a client.

cases.title: A non-coder's Claude Code tool analysed 776 videos in an afternoon
cases.summary: A thumbnail research task used to take three full days of manual work. Claude Code built a tool analysing 776 videos across 57 channels to find what worked, one of four tools a non-coder built in three weeks.
cases.result: Also rebuilt their website in under an hour
cases.prompt: Point [Claude Code] at your folder of [video/channel data] and describe the analysis in plain English, for example: 'Analyse these videos across these channels and identify thumbnail best practices,' or 'Pull action items from these emails and organise them.' Keep iterating by describing what to change until the output looks right.

cases.title: An old MacBook Air became an OpenClaw "agent box"
cases.summary: An agent box, not a primary laptop: OpenClaw runs on an old MacBook Air, reached through Slack. Its first job, a morning brief with weather, tasks and ideas, came with one broken part: the subreddit scan.
cases.result: Putting it in charge of growing a new Substack
cases.prompt: Set up a personal agent like [OpenClaw] on a dedicated always-on machine, connected through [Slack or Telegram]. Ask it: 'Send me a morning brief every day with the local weather, a few trending videos about [your interests], my open to-do list tasks, tasks you can take off my plate, and trending stories in [your interests].' Start with one feature, confirm it works, then add tool connections one at a time.

cases.title: Nap-trapped by a baby, they got Codex to build a song in Ableton
cases.summary: Nap-trapped by their baby, they built an MCP bridge so an agent could run their Ableton Live set directly. Codex composed an EDM track from scratch, then they revised vocals, drums and dynamics with follow up prompts.
cases.result: Also had Codex compose a piano duet debating AI's merits
cases.prompt: Set up an MCP bridge for your DAW, then ask your agent to build a track from scratch: specify the genre, instrumentation, and any text to speech vocals you want, e.g. '[a self reflective song with chiptunes and 80s drum machines]'. After the first draft, give focused follow up prompts one at a time, like '[add more dynamics after the drop]' or '[the vocals are squished, give them more length]', until the mix sounds right.

cases.title: Played thinking aloud, then Claude checked each thought with Stockfish
cases.summary: A recorded rapid chess game came with a voice memo of what the player was thinking move by move. Claude drove Stockfish to question each thought and built a narrated video explaining the mistakes.
cases.result: Answered the exact question asked aloud at move eight
cases.prompt: Install the chess-analysis and chess-video skills in Claude Code, then say: analyze this game: [lichess link], here is my think-aloud recording: [path to audio file]. After it finishes, ask: make a video of this game.

cases.title: A Raspberry Pi car assistant answers by voice, no internet needed
cases.summary: A Raspberry Pi rides in the car and runs a local AI model that answers spoken questions through the car's own speakers, even with the internet switched off. It also posts engine faults into the household chat room.
cases.result: Dashboard command closed a real open car window
cases.prompt: Set up a [Raspberry Pi] running a local open-weight language model through [llama.cpp], add voice input and output with [whisper.cpp] and a local text-to-speech engine, load your [vehicle owner's manual] as a retrieval source, connect a [Bluetooth OBD-II adapter] for live engine data, and have it join your household's chat app as a named agent that posts engine and fault updates on its own.

cases.title: A homemade agent turns vet charges into ready-to-send insurance claims
cases.summary: Vet bills mean a paper chase of card charges, emailed invoices and insurer forms. A homemade agent matches each charge to its Gmail invoice, fills the claim form with Gemini's help and stages a draft. A person hits send.
cases.result: Its own invoice-request emails once false-matched 12 claims
cases.prompt: Build a personal agent that watches your bank statement for a recurring category of charge, such as [vet visits], searches your email for the matching invoice, extracts the needed fields with [an LLM such as Gemini], fills the relevant PDF claim form, and stages a ready-to-send email draft in your inbox for you to review and send yourself, rather than sending anything automatically.

cases.title: 40 strangers, one conference: Claude Code built the briefing
cases.summary: Before a conference with 40 people they had never met, LinkedIn research normally takes an evening. Claude Code researched the attendees in parallel via LinkedIn and Chrome MCP, producing a full briefing in 5 minutes.
cases.result: Also books flights and hotels in the company travel system
cases.prompt: Give Claude Code a list of names for an upcoming event, such as [conference attendees] or [meeting participants]. Connect it to your LinkedIn via Chrome MCP and ask it to research each person in parallel, then compile everything into one briefing document for you to review before the event.

cases.title: Claude applied for 50 jobs in less than 30 minutes
cases.summary: Applying to jobs one by one eats hours. Using the new Claude Computer Use, 50 job applications went out in less than 30 minutes.
cases.result: Doubled as a first test of Claude's new Computer Use tool
cases.prompt: With Claude Computer Use enabled, give it your resume and a list of [job posting links]. Ask it to open each posting and fill in the application with your details and tailored answers, then show you each completed application for approval before it submits anything and moves on to the next link.

cases.title: OpenClaw read 15+ pull requests to recommend an upgrade
cases.summary: When a new OpenClaw beta added Telegram message streaming, they asked their agent what else had changed. It read 15+ merged pull requests, compared them to the current version, and gave an upgrade recommendation.
cases.result: Costs about $10-15 a day, with spikes to $30+
cases.prompt: Ask your coding or personal agent to check its own project's GitHub repository for recent merged pull requests since [your installed version], compare them to what you're currently running, and give you a plain-language summary with a recommendation on whether to upgrade.

cases.title: Devin's first PR took 10 minutes. Its 150 credits lasted under a week
cases.summary: A client's CRM needed a new deals feature. Devin opened a first pull request in under 10 minutes, but its PRs carried unneeded changes, it gave a false answer about a library, and it hit its usage limit.
cases.result: Said a library wasn't used elsewhere when it actually was
cases.prompt: Connect [your coding agent] to your project's GitHub repositories and give it the schema for a new feature, such as [feature name]. Let it break a large task into smaller sessions if needed, open a pull request for each piece, and double check its claims about existing code, such as which libraries are already used, before merging.

cases.title: Claude Cowork turned a meal-prep video into a stocked grocery cart
cases.summary: Watching a meal-prep video and building a shopping list by hand ate up time each week. Claude Cowork extracted the recipes, matched ingredients to past-invoice brands, filled the cart, and saved the recipes to Notion.
cases.result: Matched an exact oat milk brand from a past invoice
cases.prompt: Give [your agent] a link to a meal-prep video and ask it to: extract the recipes and ingredients, build a shopping list, match items to brands from your past grocery invoices in [your invoices folder], add everything to your cart on [your grocery site] without checking out, and offer alternatives for anything unavailable. Then have it save the recipes to a new page in [Notion or your notes app].

cases.title: Hermes Agent wrote, sang and made a whole 8D music video
cases.summary: An 8D music video with millions of views sparked a test: could an agent make one? Hermes Agent wrote the lyrics and music, made visuals from the song and added the 8D effect and audio-responsive video.
cases.result: It even sang the vocals
cases.prompt: Act as a music video producer. Write lyrics and an original [genre] track about [theme], export the stems, generate visuals that match the song's mood, apply an [8D audio] effect, and make the visuals react to the audio. Show me the lyrics and a short sample before rendering the full video.

cases.title: Claude wrote a test harness for a bug no one wanted to chase
cases.summary: A rabbitmq connector occasionally got stuck after rare network drops, too minor to spend days fixing. Claude built a test harness that reproduced it, and the actual fix wasn't too hard.
cases.result: Automatically runnable scenarios, not a one-off check
cases.prompt: Write a test harness that reliably reproduces [the intermittent bug], covering [the rare conditions that trigger it], so I can create automatically runnable scenarios before attempting a fix.

cases.title: OpenClaw scans used bookstores against a Goodreads list
cases.summary: Wanting their son to grow up around books, they hooked OpenClaw to their Goodreads list to scan local used bookstores for titles to buy. They say they've never read as much or enjoyed it as much as now.
cases.result: Credits it entirely to a wall of books by the chair

cases.title: Repaste a CPU, swap a PSU, snake a sink: ChatGPT walked it through

cases.title: Months of debugging by hand; Claude found each issue in a few minutes

cases.title: 1-2 weeks with Claude recreated the core of a $250k/year platform

Walk me through testing it safely before I install it as my default audio driver.

cases.title: One prompt built a real-time caffeine tracker with Claude
cases.summary: Wanting to know how much caffeine was in their system, they asked Claude to build an app: log a coffee's volume with a button, and watch the caffeine load rise then decay in real time. One shot.
cases.result: Modeled real-time caffeine decay, not just intake
cases.prompt: I want to track [caffeine] in my system from my [coffee] habit. Build me a small app with a button to log each [coffee]'s volume, that shows my current [caffeine] load and lets it decay over time automatically. Keep it simple, just a single page I can open and tap.
